parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, derived from absorbēns (“absorbing”) + -ia (“abstract noun suffix”), equivalent to absorvente + -ia. Absorbentia exists as a real word in Latin, but only as a form of the participle absorbēns. Doublet of absorvância, a partial calque of English absorbancy. Cognate with Aragonese, As

parole.significato: capitellum (rounded eminence in the head of some bones)
parole.testo: From Latin capitellum, likely by influence of English capitellum. Doublet of capitel, coudel, cabedelo, caudilho, and cadete.
From a root of Latin crux (“cross”). The sense of "crucial" is a semantic loan from English crucial.
Learned borrowing from Latin cultus. Noun sense 4 is a semantic loan from English cult.
Borrowed from Latin dēprecārī (“to avert, to ward off, to deprecate”). The computing sense is a calque of English deprecate.
Borrowed from Latin historia with influence of English story.

parole.significato: English or American pound, a unit of mass equal to 454 g
parole.testo: From Latin libra (“Roman pound”). Doublet of arrátel. In reference to the English unit, a calque of English pound. Cognate with Galician and Spanish libra and Catalan lliura.

parole.significato: medium (a person who contacts the dead)
parole.testo: Ultimately from Latin medium (“middle”), via English medium or French médium. Doublet of meio and médio.
From Orco, from Latin Orcus (“god of the underworld”). Doublet of ogro and orc. The sense of mythological creature is a semantic loan from English orc.

parole.significato: American or English inch, a unit of length equal to 2.54 cm
parole.testo: From Old Galician-Portuguese polegada, from Vulgar Latin *pollicāta, unit of length derived from Latin pollex (“thumb”). Compare Galician and Spanish pulgada. As an English unit, a calque of English inch.
From sub- (“under, below”) + Latin līmen (“threshold”) (genitive līminis) + -ar (“adjective”), a calque of English subliminal.
Uncertain. Probably from Latin situs (“position, place, site”). The Internet sense is a semantic loan from English site.
Borrowed from New Latin sodium, from Italian soda.

parole.significato: transition (process of change from one form, state, style or place to another)
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Latin trānsitiōnem (“transit; passage”), from trānseō (“to traverse”). Semantic loan from English transition in genetics and LGBT senses.

parole.significato: tractor (a type of vehicle used in farms)
parole.testo: From earlier tractor, formed from Latin tractus (“dragged”) + the suffix -or, or borrowed from English tractor.

parole.significato: to come (to move towards the speaker or the agent)
parole.testo: From Old Galician-Portuguese viir~vĩir, from Latin venīre. The sense of “to achieve orgasm” is probably a semantic loan from English come.
